title: Reading a container's boundary before claiming an escape
prerequisites: command execution inside a container or other sandboxed workload
the ability to read the workload's own view of its mounts, capabilities and namespace
excerpt: Root inside a container is not root on the host: before calling anything an escape, read what the workload itself can see — mounted host paths, an exposed container-runtime socket, granted Linux capabilities beyond the default set, a shared process or network namespace, credentials for the orchestrator's own API. Each of these is a boundary question, not a boundary crossing; the runtime's default configuration already denies most of them. The effect worth proving is an operation that only succeeds because the boundary was absent — a file written outside the container, a command run as the host's own init — observed from outside the workload, not a privileged prompt still inside it.
